Who We Are
In order to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, we must trailblaze the path and shape the future of our industry. This is something our employees work at each day and is defined by our values: Disruption, Collaboration, Execution, Integrity, and Inclusion. We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!
We believe collaboration thrives in person. That’s why most of our teams work from the office full time, with flexibility when it’s needed. This model supports real-time problem-solving, stronger relationships, and the kind of precision that drives great outcomes.
Job Summary
As a Staff Software Engineer in IT Quality Engineering Automation, you will be the technical anchor and visionary for our automated testing and next-generation SDLC ecosystem, operating directly from our Bangalore office. At Palo Alto Networks, we are transitioning from traditional QA to an AI-First engineering culture.
We are looking for an early-in-career AI Engineer to build and ship custom Agentic AI. Applications across an Enterprise IT landscape spanning Salesforce, SAP, custom. Licensing and Entitlement management applications, and AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning and ITSM platforms. You will work with modern generative AI — LLM orchestration, autonomous agent loops, tool calling and RAG — against real enterprise infrastructure, building agents that carry out multi-step business workflows, act on data across these systems through their APIs, and hand back to a human when they should.
At Palo Alto Networks we are moving towards an AI-First engineering culture, and you will not be starting from a blank page. You will build on our own internal AI platform tools for test generation, automation scripting, execution and quality reporting.
Agentic Systems & Enterprise Integration
Build agentic features: Develop and maintain agent workflows using LangGraph, ADK, LangChain, AutoGen or CrewAI, including planner/executor loops, state handling and failure recovery.
Enable cross-system integration and tool calling: Connect agents across enterprise applications, including: Salesforce: REST/SOAP APIs, Webhooks, Platform Events, Apex Invocable Methods, SOQL and Flows. SAP: OData/BAPI services and business-object events. Custom applications: Licensing, Entitlement, AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning and ITSM through REST APIs, webhooks and message queues.
Build context grounding and RAG pipelines: Use vector stores such as pgvector, Pinecone and Weaviate to provide LLMs with accurate, current enterprise context.
Define tools and schemas: Create well-specified tool definitions and JSON function schemas, including MCP tools, to support deterministic tool calls and traceability back to Jira.
Agent Quality, Safety & Observability
Build evaluation suites: Develop and run golden-set evaluations to validate improvements to agents and prompts before release.
Implement guardrails and human-in-the-loop workflows: Establish safety controls, rate limiting, fallbacks and clear approval handoffs, especially when agents write to systems of record.
Enable observability: Instrument agents with tracing and metrics covering execution paths, latency, context usage and token costs, and use findings to improve performance.
Apply responsible AI practices: Follow company policies on intellectual property and data privacy, keep secrets in managed stores and require explicit opt-in for steps that send content to external services.
Collaboration & Growth
Collaborate across functions: Partner with Salesforce, SAP and platform architects, QE leads, product managers and security teams to deliver reliable AI features that meet business, quality and enterprise compliance requirements.
Learn the enterprise landscape: Build an understanding of transaction flows from AI Custom Quoting and order capture through licensing, entitlement, provisioning and service management. Prior knowledge is not required, but proactive learning is expected.
Share knowledge: Contribute working examples, reusable tools and reviewed code to strengthen AI fluency across engineering teams.
Qualifications
Experience: 1–4 years of professional software engineering experience or equivalent demonstrable capability.
Programming: Strong proficiency in Python or TypeScript/Node.js, with sound fundamentals in data structures, testing and code review.
Backend fundamentals: Practical experience building and consuming REST APIs, working with relational databases and handling asynchronous or queue-based processing.
Hands-on LLM experience: Demonstrable experience with LLM APIs, including prompting, function/tool calling and structured outputs, through professional work, internships, open-source contributions or substantial personal projects.
Agentic or RAG exposure: Built at least one working agent or retrieval pipeline end to end, with the ability to explain its design, failures and improvements.
Integration skills: Comfortable reading unfamiliar enterprise API documentation and determining how to integrate safely.
Version control and CI: Comfortable using Git in a team environment and working with automated build and test pipelines.
AI-assisted development: Daily working fluency with tools such as Cursor, Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, with the judgement to critically review generated output.
Education: B.E./B.Tech/M.Tech in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Production agents: Experience deploying AI agents or LLM features into production, including multi-agent coordination or autonomous decision loops.
Enterprise application knowledge: Exposure to one or more of the following: Salesforce: REST/Composite/Bulk APIs, SOQL/SOSL, Connected Apps, OAuth and Apex. SAP: OData, BAPI/RFC, IDocs or business-object events. Enterprise platforms: AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning, Licensing/Entitlement or ITSM platforms and their supporting distributed services.
Vector databases and embeddings: Experience with semantic search, embedding generation and vector engines such as pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant or ChromaDB.
Advanced retrieval: Familiarity with Graph RAG, Corrective RAG, HyDE or agentic retrieval, and graph stores such as Apache AGE or Neo4j.
Model Context Protocol: Experience authoring MCP servers, including tools, resources and prompts.
Cloud and DevOps: Exposure to GCP, AWS or Azure, containerisation using Docker or Kubernetes, and serverless computing. Vertex AI experience is a plus.
Test automation: Familiarity with Playwright, REST Assured, Selenium or PyTest.
Domain interest: Grounding in B2B sales processes, Partner Relationship Management (PRM) or the Quote-to-Cash lifecycle.
Ways of Working
Evidence over assertion: Measure results before and after changes, share findings with the methodology and clearly acknowledge inconclusive outcomes.
Curiosity with rigour: Explore new tools, validate them before adoption and understand the difference between a demo and a reliable system.
Ownership: Take tasks from ambiguity through delivery and raise blockers early.
Builder’s bias: Prioritise shipping focused, reliable capabilities that users can trust over broad features that only perform well in demonstrations.
Growth Path
Join at the AI Engineer tier of the internal AI capability ladder, between AI User and AI Architect.
Progress towards AI Architect, building expertise in: Planner–executor orchestration at scale. Multi-agent systems with human-in-the-loop controls. Event-driven integration across enterprise IT systems. Model customisation.
Access company-funded training to support this progression.
The Team
Join a growing, passionate and dynamic team working on challenging, mission-driven projects.
Contribute to a people-centric culture focused on creating an exceptional employee experience.
Help expand what is possible in the workplace through innovation and collaboration
Our Commitment
We’re trailblazers that dream big, take risks, and challenge cybersecurity’s status quo. It’s simple: we can’t accomplish our mission without diverse teams innovating, together.

About the Role
We are looking for a Staff AI Engineer to be the technical anchor for Agentic AI in IT Quality Engineering – setting the architecture, standards and roadmap for custom Agentic AI applications across an Enterprise IT landscape spanning Salesforce, SAP, custom Licensing and Entitlement management applications, and AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning and ITSM platforms. You will decide how agents plan, act, retrieve context and hand back to a human across these systems; how they are evaluated, governed and operated in production; and how the wider engineering team builds them well. This is a hands-on role: you will still design and write the hardest parts yourself.
At Palo Alto Networks we are moving towards an AI-First engineering culture. You will shape the direction of our own internal AI platform tools for test generation, automation scripting, execution and quality reporting, and lead the engineers who build on them.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Architecture & Technical Direction
Agentic Architecture: Define the reference architecture for agentic systems across the landscape — planner-executor orchestration, multi-agent coordination, state, memory and recovery — and choose frameworks such as LangGraph, ADK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen or CrewAI on evidence rather than fashion.
Event-Driven Enterprise Integration: Architect event-driven pipelines that connect Salesforce (Platform Events, Change Data Capture, Apex, Flows), SAP (OData/BAPI services and business-object events) and custom Licensing, Entitlement, AI Custom Quoting, Provisioning and ITSM applications to AI processing with production OAuth2 lifecycle, least-privilege access and idempotent writes to systems of record.
Context & Knowledge Architecture: Set the retrieval strategy across the estate — vector and graph stores (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate or Milvus; Apache AGE or Neo4j), advanced topologies (Graph RAG, Corrective RAG, HyDE, agentic retrieval), and the ingestion, freshness and access-control rules that keep context correct.
Tool & Protocol Standards: Own the standards for tool definitions, JSON function schemas and MCP servers across teams, so that agent tool calls are schema-validated, auditable and traceable back to Jira.
Model Strategy: Decide when prompting and retrieval are enough and when model customisation is justified — and lead resource-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA) where it is.
Quality, Safety & Governance at Scale
Evaluation Strategy & Release Gates: Define how AI agents — ours and the ones other teams build that the business depends on — are evaluated before release: golden sets, calibrated LLM-as-judge, adversarial testing, and risk-tiered release gates that block what should be blocked.
Autonomy & HITL Governance: Set the autonomy model — which decisions an agent may take alone, which need human approval, and how that changes as evidence accumulates — and make sure it is enforced in code, especially where agents write to systems of record.
LLMOps & Platform Reliability: Architect secure AI gateways, token-budget and rate-limit controls, model deployment pipelines, drift monitoring and automated rollback; own service levels, cost and incident response for production agents.
Responsible AI & Data Governance: Partner with security and data-governance owners to define guardrails on intellectual property and data privacy — managed secrets, explicit opt-in for any step that sends content to an external service, and an audit trail a reviewer can follow.
Leadership & Influence
Design & Review Board: Lead design reviews for agentic and AI-integrated systems across Salesforce, SAP and custom platforms, and set the code and design standards for both human-written and AI-generated code.
Roadmap & Strategy: Partner with engineering leadership, QE leads, product managers and enterprise architects to turn quality and business goals into a sequenced AI engineering roadmap — and say plainly what will not work.
Mentorship & Capability Building: Mentor Senior AI Engineers and AI Engineers, grow the next AI Architects, and shape the reference implementations and training that move engineers up our AI capability ladder.
Cross-Organisation Influence: Represent IT Quality Engineering in enterprise architecture and AI governance forums, and drive adoption of AI-native engineering practice beyond your own team.
Qualifications
Required Skills & Experience
Experience: 7–10 years of professional software engineering experience, including 3+ years in applied AI/ML, of which at least 2 years building LLM-based or agentic systems that reached production.
Leadership Track Record: 2+ years as a technical lead, staff engineer or architect driving architectural decisions and leading cross-functional technical initiatives to production.
Programming Mastery: Expert proficiency in Python and strong proficiency in Java or TypeScript/Node.js; excellent software design is a given.
Agentic Systems Architecture: You have designed and led production agentic systems — planner-executor orchestration, multi-agent coordination, state and memory, HITL control — and can explain the trade-offs you made and what you would change.
Distributed & Event-Driven Systems: Deep experience with microservices, event-driven architecture and message queues (e.g., Kafka, Pub/Sub), including idempotency, ordering, back-pressure and failure recovery.
Retrieval at Scale: You have designed production RAG systems over vector and/or graph stores, including access-controlled ingestion and measured retrieval quality.
Evaluation & Governance: You have established evaluation and release-gating practice for LLM systems — golden sets, LLM-as-judge calibration, adversarial and prompt-injection testing — that was adopted beyond your own team.
Enterprise Integration: Deep experience integrating with enterprise platforms — Salesforce, SAP or comparable CRM, ERP or ITSM systems — including OAuth2 lifecycle, safe write patterns and data-governance constraints.
Cloud, LLMOps & CI/CD: Strong experience with GCP/AWS/Azure, Docker and Kubernetes, CI/CD at enterprise scale, and operating AI services with observability, cost controls and rollback.
AI-Assisted Development: Deep fluency with tools such as Cursor, Claude Code or GitHub Copilot, and a track record of setting team practice for reviewing what they produce.
Education: B.E./B.Tech/M.Tech in Computer Science, Computer Engineering or a related technical field (or equivalent practical experience).
Preferred Qualifications
Model Customisation: Hands-on fine-tuning with resource-efficient methods (LoRA/QLoRA), including data preparation and evaluation of the tuned model against its base.
Integration Platforms: Event-driven enterprise integration in practice — SAP business-object events and workflow triggers, Salesforce Platform Events or Change Data Capture, and middleware such as SnapLogic or MuleSoft.
Model Context Protocol: Designing MCP server estates used across teams — tools, resources and prompts, with versioning and access control.
Managed AI Platforms: Production experience with Vertex AI or an equivalent managed AI platform.
AI Security: Threat modelling for agentic systems — prompt injection, tool misuse, data exfiltration and red-teaming practice.
Quality Engineering at Scale: Architecting test automation or quality platforms (Playwright, REST Assured, Selenium or PyTest), including AI-assisted test generation or self-healing automation.
Domain Expertise: Deep grounding in B2B sales, Partner Relationship Management (PRM), the Quote-to-Cash lifecycle, or licensing, entitlement and provisioning flows.
Industry Contribution: Publications, conference talks or significant open-source contributions in agentic AI, retrieval or LLM evaluation.
WAYS OF WORKING
Evidence over Assertion: You measure before and after, you publish the number with its method attached, you say plainly when a result is inconclusive — and you hold the team's claims to the same standard.
Curiosity with Rigour: You enjoy new tooling but you test it before you trust it, and you know the difference between a demo and a system.
Strategic Influence: You change direction with evidence and clear writing rather than authority, with technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.
High Autonomy: You take ambiguous, cross-system problems and turn them into a plan a team can execute, and you raise risks early rather than late.
Builder's Bias: You would rather ship a narrow capability that works and is trusted than a broad one that only demos well — and you set that standard for the team.
GROWTH PATH
This role sits at the AI Architect tier of our internal AI capability ladder (AI User → AI Engineer → AI Architect), and you will operate there from the start: planner-executor orchestration at scale, multi-agent systems with human-in-the-loop control, event-driven integration across the enterprise IT landscape, and model customisation. From here the role grows in scope from a single programme to the AI engineering direction of IT Quality Engineering — and in the number of engineers you bring up the same ladder.
THE TEAM
You will be part of a growing, passionate and dynamic team, with the opportunity to work on challenging and exciting projects centred on what we believe is one of the most significant mission statements in the world. We also strive to be the most people-centric company ever — that means we are constantly working to make your experience amazing, and you are part of the team breaking the boundaries of what the workplace can be.

An overview of this role
Help us build the next generation of authentication services at GitLab. As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Authentication team, you'll build authentication features across the Rails monolith and GATE. GATE is our new service for issuing and validating tokens and managing identities, designed to support every GitLab deployment model.
You'll expand authentication mechanisms, including support for identities used by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. You'll also help keep GitLab and its customers secure by building access management tooling and addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.
GATE will become the foundation for token issuance, validation, and identity services across GitLab.com multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS), Self-Managed, Dedicated, and air-gapped environments. Your work will affect core components that customers, users, and GitLab teams rely on.
Some of our projects include:
Building GATE as the centralized service for token issuance and validation
Consolidating tokens and migrating authentication paths out of the Rails monolith
Building passkeys and passwordless authentication
Developing composite identities that combine machine and human authorization for AI
Improving service accounts and secure automation
Enhancing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) capabilities for automated user provisioning and single sign-on (SSO)
What you'll do
Shape the roadmap for GATE and GitLab's authentication services with the team.
Design and implement token issuance, validation, and identity services in Go and Ruby across the Rails monolith and GATE, including new authentication mechanisms such as Workload Identity Federation.
Migrate authentication and token management paths from the monolith into GATE while maintaining reliability across all deployment models.
Build authentication mechanisms from the ground up, such as Workload Identity Federation.
Strengthen security for users and organizations through access management tooling and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.
Define and improve standards for style, maintainability, and engineering practices in a high-scale environment, and advocate for them through code review.
Communicate publicly about GitLab initiatives, projects, and contributions from people not working for GitLab Inc. Reflect GitLab's values in these communications.
Ship moderately sized features and improvements with moderate guidance and support from other team members, and collaborate on larger projects, including the build-out of GATE.
Participate in the maintainer trainee program at your own comfortable pace while working toward becoming a project maintainer.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Professional experience with Go and/or Ruby in scaling or mission-critical SaaS products.
Familiarity with authentication and authorization technologies or techniques, such as OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SSO, SCIM, LDAP, JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), role-based access control (RBAC), or identity and access management (IAM).
Knowledge of token systems, cryptographic signing, and key management.
Experience building or contributing to a service from concept to production, including proposal, discussion, and execution.
Proficiency in written and verbal English, with the ability to communicate complex problems and solutions clearly in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.
Experience diagnosing, preventing, and resolving performance and optimization problems.
Experience working in an iterative software development process, managing your work effectively, staying organized, and following through on priorities.
About the team
Our mission is to empower GitLab system administrators with the toolkit they need to create their desired balance of security and accessibility for their GitLab experience.
Authentication is the first impression a new customer has when they configure a new GitLab instance. We aim to make it as seamless as possible, from that first login to onboarding users and managing security rules for their instance in a secure, flexible, and scalable way.

A ChatOps feature that makes it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com

Advocate for and drive improvements to support practices, product quality, and reusable documentation and support content that directly influence team objectives.

As a Staff Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) at GitLab, you’ll help keep all user-facing services and production systems reliable, scalable, and efficient. Our SREs combine a pragmatic operations mindset with strong software engineering practices to drive automation, reduce toil, and improve resilience across our platform.
In the Environment Automation specialization, your focus is on operating and automating hundreds of GitLab environments—from initial provisioning to day-to-day maintenance tasks. 
Unlike other SRE roles, this position centers on automating the lifecycle of many tenant environments, ensuring they remain secure, consistent, and reliable at scale.
Some examples of the projects you could work on:
Designing infrastructure automation that provisions and operates GitLab environments using Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes
Creating and maintaining deployment packages for GitLab, such as Helm Charts and omnibus-gitlab
Building and operating Dedicated GitLab instances integrated with cloud-native services (e.g., GCP, AWS)
Developing tools to orchestrate infrastructure-as-code workflows across multiple tenants
Deploying and managing microservices on Kubernetes clusters at scale
Enhancing GitLab’s observability stack (e.g., Prometheus, ELK) to support proactive monitoring and incident response
Integrating with and operating infrastructure in cloud provider ecosystems (e.g., IAM, networking, storage)
Championing and implementing cloud security best practices across automated infrastructure
What You’ll Do
Build & Scale Multi-Tenant Infrastructure: Design and implement automation that provisions and manages hundreds of isolated GitLab environments using Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes. Manage complex state strategies and workspace configurations to support scale and maintainability.
Debug & Resolve Production Issues: Troubleshoot issues across Kubernetes clusters, cloud services, and GitLab apps—identifying root causes of failed deployments, crash loops, and scheduling conflicts to ensure service continuity.
Automate Operations at Scale: Replace manual workflows with infrastructure-as-code solutions, including automated version upgrades, configuration rollouts, and provisioning pipelines that operate reliably across all tenants.
Monitor & Predict Capacity: Build observability systems that detect bottlenecks, predict usage trends, and optimize resource consumption using tools like Prometheus, ELK, and Grafana.
Respond & Lead During Incidents: Lead incident response and postmortem efforts, applying technical depth to resolve issues and establish operational standards that reduce future risk.
Architect & Collaborate: Influence architectural decisions around automation, scalability, and operational excellence. Partner with engineering teams to improve automation, platform resilience, and production-readiness.
On Call Support: Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What You’ll Bring
Production-Scale Experience: Proven ability to operate and troubleshoot production workloads across multiple tenants or environments. Deep understanding of how distributed systems fail at scale and how to build in resilience.
Terraform & IaC Mastery: Strong hands-on experience with Terraform, including workspace strategies, state management, and automation patterns that scale. Comfortable solving state isolation issues and building reliable, reusable infrastructure code. Experience with Ansible and templating tools like Jsonnet is a plus.
Kubernetes in Production: Skilled at diagnosing deployment failures, interpreting pod logs, and debugging scheduling issues and rollback scenarios in live environments. Understands how pods, ReplicaSets, and controllers interact in production.
Programming & Code Analysis: Ability to read and debug code in Go and/or Ruby. Familiar with identifying performance issues, scalability concerns, and contributing to infrastructure tooling through thoughtful code analysis.
Large Scale Operations Background: Experience supporting infrastructure for many customers or environments simultaneously. Comfortable managing isolation, scaling, monitoring, and incident response across diverse workloads.
Architecture & Incident Response: Able to reason through complex systems and operational challenges. Brings on-call experience and can lead technical discussions and incident resolution efforts under pressure.
Customer-Focused Collaboration: Proven ability to work across teams and with internal or external customers to solve technical problems while maintaining service commitments and clear communication.
GitLab Platform Proficiency: Comfortable using GitLab as a daily tool for infrastructure automation, collaboration, and operational workflows.
About the team
GitLab’s Dedicated team, where the SRE Environment Automation role sits, is on a mission to deliver a fully managed, single-tenant GitLab experience through the GitLab Dedicated platform. Our goal is to eliminate manual operations across the entire lifecycle of customer environments, including provisioning, upgrades, security, and monitoring, so customers can focus on unlocking the full potential of The One DevOps Platform without managing the underlying infrastructure. We build scalable, automated systems that ensure each GitLab Dedicated instance is secure, consistent, and production-ready—whether we're managing 10 environments or hundreds.

Develop reconciliation and data integrity checks across usage and billing pipelines.
Define and track service level objectives and service level indicators, write runbooks, and take part in incident response to measure and improve Monetization system reliability.
Explore artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to predict system anomalies and accelerate resolution.
Review and offer feedback on merge requests from other Monetization engineers.
Collaborate with Product, Finance, Support, and other partners to turn operational needs into reliable tooling.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

Professional experience with Ruby on Rails, including building and operating applications such as CustomersDot.
Experience in site reliability or observability engineering, including monitoring, alerting, service level objectives and indicators, runbooks, and incident response.
Experience setting technical direction for observability, reliability, or detection work and bringing other engineers along.
Experience building anomaly detection, monitoring, or risk management tooling.
Familiarity with observability tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry.

An overview of this role
As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.
Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.
We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.
What you'll do
Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

We're an OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for millions of users. We also accept identity from enterprise identity providers through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Behind that sit more than ten token types and several session methods that grew inside the Ruby on Rails monolith. You'll help us move this work onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. GATE exchanges external credentials for short-lived tokens at the edge through a Secure Token Service written in Go.You'll set our technical direction, lead the hardest protocol and migration work yourself, and help senior engineers own the rest.
Our projects include:
OAuth across Cells: Making OAuth clients, grants, and tokens work when users and organizations live in different cells
Global identities: One user identity that works across organizations and cells
Token consolidation: Reducing the number of token types and moving token issuance and validation out of the monolith
Identity for artificial intelligence (AI) agents and workloads: OAuth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, workload identity federation, and service identities with narrow scopes
What you'll do
Own the technical direction for authentication protocols at GitLab, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and token exchange, across the Rails monolith and GATE services.
Write and drive design documents and architecture decision records (ADRs) for multi-quarter work, then break that work into increments that ship behind feature flags.
Lead migrations that must not break existing customers: token formats, client and grant state, and session behavior on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.
Be hands-on in the most complex parts of the code, in Ruby on Rails and Go, and review the designs and merge requests of other engineers.
Agree interface contracts with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams, and keep them current as the architecture changes.
Treat authentication as a security and availability boundary: threat-model new flows, add rate limits and abuse controls, and lead the technical response to authentication incidents.
Mentor senior and intermediate engineers on the team and raise the protocol and security knowledge of the whole group.
Work asynchronously with engineers in India, Europe, and the Americas, with most decisions made in writing.
Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.
What you'll bring
Significant experience building and running production authentication or identity systems at scale, with technical leadership across teams that moves unclear problems to written decisions and shipped code.
Deep, hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC: authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), refresh token rotation, token exchange, client registration, scopes, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) with signing keys and key rotation.
Working knowledge of SAML 2.0 single sign-on and enterprise identity integration (LDAP, System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or similar).
Strong production experience in Ruby on Rails or Go, willingness to work in both, and experience with careful refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and backward-compatible migrations in large, long-lived codebases.
A security mindset. You think about token theft, replay, revocation, and blast radius before you think about elegance.
Experience with multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS) systems, including data isolation and performance under high request volume.
Clear, concise written English and comfort working in an all-remote, asynchronous company.
Optional experience: authentication libraries (Doorkeeper, Devise, or OmniAuth), passkeys or multi-factor authentication, workload identity, gateways or policy engines, AI agent authentication, or multi-region architectures. Contributions to identity standards or open source identity projects are also welcome.
About the team
The Authentication group is part of the Security Platform stage, alongside Authorization, GATE Core, GATE Infra, Secrets Manager, and other security teams. We own sign-in, single sign-on, OAuth, and personal and service tokens. Our work touches every GitLab customer, and much of it is on the critical path for Cells and for GitLab's AI agent platform.

Job Details | Atlassian
Senior Engineering Manager- TDP Insights and Data Resiliency
Engineering | Bengaluru, India | Remote, Remote | Full-Time
Apply for this job
Working at Atlassian
Atlassians can choose where they work – whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity.
To help our teams work together effectively, this role requires you to be located in India. You will work closely with engineering teams in India and Australia and coordinate strategy, priorities, and execution with leadership in the United States.
Atlassian’s Trusted Data Platform (TDP) provides secure, reliable, and scalable data capabilities used by Atlassian product and platform teams. It helps those teams manage persistent customer data while meeting complex enterprise requirements, including data residency, encryption, regulatory compliance, backup and recovery, and operation across multiple cloud environments.
TDP Insights provides the intelligence layer for the Trusted Data Platform. It helps teams understand where data lives, how it moves, what it costs, how reliably it operates, and how customers use TDP services. By transforming high-volume platform telemetry into actionable insights, it supports better decisions about reliability, capacity, cost, compliance, recovery readiness, and developer experience.
Atlassian Data Resiliency (ADR) strengthens end-to-end recovery across TDP. It provides common backup and restore capabilities, recovery assurance, RPO and RTO evidence, validation, restore exercises, and consistent resiliency standards across TDP data platforms.
We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the TDP Insights and ADR engineering team. This leader will be accountable for the team’s people, strategy, execution, and operational outcomes. They will partner with senior engineers, product and program leaders, storage and streaming teams, infrastructure teams, security specialists, and Atlassian product organizations to improve how Atlassian understands, protects, and recovers its data.
Success in this role means building a strong engineering organization, delivering trusted platform insights and recovery capabilities, and translating complex customer, reliability, and infrastructure requirements into a clear and executable roadmap.
Team and organizational leadership
Lead, coach, and develop engineers and senior technical leaders, establishing clear expectations and accountability.
Build an inclusive, high-performing team through effective hiring, onboarding, talent development, and succession planning.
Develop senior technical and leadership talent by delegating meaningful ownership to senior engineers and emerging leaders.
Establish operating practices that support good decisions, predictable execution, and continuous improvement.
Manage capacity across strategic investments, customer commitments, operational work, and technical debt.
Build an effective distributed-team operating model across India and Australia, with clear alignment and communication with leadership in the United States.
Strategy and execution
Define and execute the TDP Insights and ADR strategy and roadmap in alignment with Atlassian’s broader data-platform and cloud-infrastructure goals.
Translate enterprise, product, platform, and recovery requirements into measurable outcomes, milestones, and engineering plans.
Surface delivery risks, cross-team dependencies, capacity constraints, and required trade-offs early.
Establish clear ownership and decision-making responsibilities across TDP Insights, ADR, TDP data platforms, and partner teams.
Deliver actionable insights into platform health, customer adoption, cost, data movement, compliance, and recovery readiness.
Improve recovery confidence through common capabilities, clear standards, validation, and repeatable restore exercises.
Reliability and customer trust
Own the operational health of TDP Insights and ADR capabilities, including availability, data quality, performance, security, compliance, and recoverability.
Establish service-level objectives, operational indicators, review mechanisms, and sustainable on-call practices.
Establish trustworthy measures for backup coverage, restore validation, RPO and RTO performance, and recovery readiness.
Lead the response to material incidents and ensure that lessons produce durable technical and organizational improvements.
Ensure that TDP Insights and ADR support enterprise needs such as data residency, encryption, disaster recovery, regulated environments, and multi-cloud operation.
Maintain clear visibility into customer and recovery commitments and intervene when delivery, reliability, or data-integrity risks threaten those outcomes.
Technical and platform leadership
Partner with senior technical leaders to establish architectural direction and make high-quality technical decisions.
Guide the evolution of large-scale telemetry, analytics, backup, restore, and recovery capabilities across multiple cloud providers and specialized operating environments.
Ensure designs account for scalability, data locality, security, compliance, data quality, migration safety, operability, and reversibility.
Establish technical and operational standards for data collection, processing, analytics, recovery validation, and integration with TDP data platforms.
Balance near-term delivery with platform simplification, lifecycle management, cloud portability, and reduction of operational burden.
Establish clear technical and operational contracts with storage, streaming, control-plane, infrastructure, and customer teams.
Cross-functional leadership and economics
Build trusted partnerships across product, engineering, security, compliance, reliability, infrastructure, FinOps, and customer-facing teams.
Coordinate effectively across engineering teams in India and Australia and leadership stakeholders in the United States.
Resolve cross-organizational dependencies through explicit owners, acceptance criteria, and delivery dates.
Represent TDP Insights and ADR in engineering reviews, leadership forums, operational reviews, architecture discussions, and portfolio planning.
Use platform telemetry and operational evidence to inform investment, reliability, capacity, and customer-adoption decisions.
Own the cost posture of the team’s capabilities, including infrastructure efficiency, demand forecasting, unit economics, and cost attribution.
Make investment decisions that prioritize customer trust, strategic platform value, and sustainable cost efficiency.
Minimum qualifications:
Significant engineering leadership experience.
Demonstrated success building or operating a business-critical distributed system, data platform, analytics platform, storage service, resiliency platform, or comparable infrastructure product.
Strong people leadership skills, including coaching, performance management, organizational design, hiring, and succession planning.
Experience converting ambiguous strategies and customer requirements into clear roadmaps, execution plans, and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of distributed systems, data platforms, cloud infrastructure, reliability engineering, security, and operational risk.
Experience operating large-scale production systems with clear service-level objectives, observability, incident management, capacity planning, and sustainable operational practices.
Experience delivering enterprise capabilities such as data residency, encryption, compliance, backup and recovery, disaster recovery, or tenant isolation.
Proven ability to lead incident response and convert operational learning into lasting improvements.
Strong cross-functional influence and experience resolving dependencies between organizations with different priorities.
Experience leading teams and programs across multiple geographies and time zones.
Sound judgment when balancing reliability, strategic alignment, delivery speed, cost, and technical sustainability.
Clear communication skills appropriate for engineers, executives, product partners, and customer-facing stakeholders.
Experience with high-scale telemetry and analytics systems, streaming and data-processing technologies such as Kafka or Flink, analytical query platforms, distributed storage, backup and restore systems, multi-cloud infrastructure, or internal developer platforms is beneficial but not required.
Benefits & Perks
Atlassian offers a wide range of perks and benefits designed to support you, your family and to help you engage with your local community. Our offerings include health and wellbeing resources, paid volunteer days, and so much more. To learn more, visit go.atlassian.com/perksandbenefits.

At Atlassian, we're motivated by a common goal: to unleash the potential of every team. Our software products help teams all over the planet and our solutions are designed for all types of work. Team collaboration through our tools makes what may be impossible alone, possible together.

Job Details | Atlassian
Principal Security Engineer, Cloud Security
Security | Bengaluru, India | Remote, Remote
Apply for this job
Working at Atlassian
Atlassians can choose where they work - whether in an office, from home, or a combination of the two. That way, Atlassians have more control over supporting their family, personal goals, and other priorities. We can hire people in any country where we have a legal entity. Interviews and onboarding are conducted virtually, as part of being a distributed-first company.
About Team
The Product Security team at Atlassian is committed to ensuring the delivery of secure products. These teams are geographically distributed, with a presence in the USA, Australia, and India. Each team is structured uniformly to provide comprehensive product security services tailored to their respective time zones. These services include security consulting, risk identification, and mitigation consulting for all products within their purview.
Recognising the critical importance of product security as a customer necessity and a competitive edge, our team holds a pivotal position within the organisation. With Atlassian's strong engineering focus and emphasis on autonomous teams, maturing the security of this complex environment stands as our core duty. Our tasks encompass identifying potential security threats in our products, devising suitable mitigation strategies, and evaluating their effectiveness on a large scale. It is imperative to execute these responsibilities in a scalable manner, allowing us to adapt to the evolving landscape shaped by changes in our business, global dynamics, adversarial strategies, customer requirements, technological advancements, and other factors.
OverviewAs a Principal Security Engineer, Cloud Security at Atlassian, you will be the technical architect and engineer driving the architecture and technical vision across our cloud platforms, infrastructure, and software supply chain. You will partner closely with engineering leadership, platform teams, and principal architects to define secure-by-default standards, architect scalable guardrails, and lead cross - organisational initiatives that protect Atlassian’s cloud environments at global scale.
In this role, you will operate at the intersection of deep technical leadership and strategic influence - diving hands-on into complex architectural designs, critical codebases, and high-severity escalations, while steering long-term security roadmaps and mentoring senior engineers across the organization. You will systematically identify systemic risks, design resilient mitigations, and ensure our cloud platforms deliver world-class security, reliability, and trust for over 300,000+ customers.
As a Principal Product Security Engineer, Cloud Security, you will be the technical architect and engineer driving the architecture and and strategic SME driving cloud security architecture, automation, and secure-by-default platforms across Atlassian's global footprint. You will define the technical vision, establish architectural standards, and lead cross-organizational initiatives that equip engineering teams with state-of-the-art tools, patterns, and guardrails to build secure products by default. Partnering closely with security leadership, principal architects, and platform engineering teams, you will champion strategic programs that uplift and scale our security posture across multi-cloud environments. Some of your key responsibilities will include:
Strategic Architecture & Secure Design: Define and steer the overarching security architecture for multi-cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure), setting company-wide secure-by-default standards, architectural patterns, and guardrails for cloud-native services and core platforms.
Complex Threat Modeling & High-Impact Assessments: Drive advanced threat modeling and deep-dive security assessments across critical, complex systems, distributed microservices, and high-assurance environments (such as Isolated, Private, and Regulated/FedRAMP offerings).
Platform Automation & Guardrails at Scale: Architect, champion, and scale automated security controls, detection capabilities, and self-healing guardrails embedded directly into CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code (IaC), systematically eliminating classes of vulnerabilities.
Continuous Posture Optimization & CSPM Strategy: Set the technical direction for Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) and posture analytics, driving continuous compliance, maturing security baselines, and providing leadership visibility into systemic risk.
Operational & Architectural Excellence: Establish company-wide reusable security frameworks, engineering guidelines, and operational standards that improve resilience, reliability, and security performance across Atlassian products.
Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Serve as a technical sponsor and mentor for security and software engineers across the organization, fostering an inclusive culture of engineering excellence, security advocacy, and cross-team capability uplift.
Critical Incident Advisory & Architectural Remediation: Act as the principal cloud security authority during high-severity security incidents, partnering with Incident Response to conduct root-cause investigations, formulate long-term architectural mitigations, and prevent recurrence.
Executive & Stakeholder Influence: Translate complex cloud security risks and technical roadmaps into strategic priorities for executive and non-technical stakeholders, driving consensus and cross-functional alignment on mission-critical security initiatives.
On Your First Day, We'll Expect You To Have
10+ years of experience in security engineering with deep specialization in cloud security, secure architecture, and platform security at enterprise or hyper-growth SaaS scale.
Proven track record as a technical authority or principal engineer driving large-scale security architectures, risk mitigations, and threat modeling initiatives across complex SaaS and cloud-native systems.
Deep, hands-on expertise in multi-cloud security (AWS, GCP, and/or Azure) and container orchestration ecosystems (Docker, Kubernetes, service mesh).
Extensive experience designing, securing, and conducting comprehensive architectural reviews for highly regulated, high-assurance cloud environments (such as Isolated, Private, Government, and FedRAMP offerings).
Demonstrated experience guiding broad architectural transformations, including overseeing security strategy for monolith-to-microservices migrations.
Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language (such as Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript) and proven experience authoring scalable security automation, tooling, and infrastructure as code (IaC).
Deep experience embedding automated security controls, policy-as-code, and compliance gates into modern CI/CD pipelines.
Exceptional technical communication and executive influence, with a demonstrated ability to align diverse engineering teams, architects, and senior leadership around strategic security goals.
Proven track record of mentoring and coaching senior engineers and cultivating an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture.
At Atlassian, we strive to design equitable, explainable, and competitive compensation programs. We follow consistent hiring practices and account for each candidate's skills, knowledge, and experience when setting base pay within the range.
This role may also be eligible for benefits, bonuses, commissions, and equity.
Required:
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
Deep architectural mastery of cloud security, zero trust architecture, tenant data isolation, cryptographic systems/encryption, and multi-tenant SaaS environments at enterprise scale.
Proven track record designing and driving infrastructure as code (IaC) governance, centralised secrets management, and embedding automated security guardrails across the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC).
Deep understanding of cloud detection engineering, distributed telemetry/logging, IAM graph analysis, least-privilege policy automation, and enterprise alert optimisation.
Demonstrated ability to champion developer velocity and engineering experience (DevEx) while establishing robust, non-negotiable security guardrails.
Exceptional communication, technical leadership, and stakeholder influence across both executive leadership and engineering teams.
It's great, but not required if you have:
Extensive experience architecting and building scalable internal software platforms or developer tooling that automate security and compliance workflows.
Discovered and disclosed notable CVEs, or active maintainership/contributions to open-source security tooling and frameworks.
Delivered presentations at recognized industry security conferences (e.g., Black Hat, DEF CON) or published security research.
Deep hands-on experience securing modern serverless architectures, service meshes, and large-scale container orchestration platforms (Kubernetes).
Experience architecting security controls for highly regulated cloud environments (such as FedRAMP, Isolated, or Sovereign Cloud offerings).
You’ll Thrive Here If You
Take ownership of outcomes and drive projects to completion.
Are proactive in identifying and mitigating security risks.
Enjoy collaborating across teams and mentoring others.
Communicate clearly and adapt your message to your audience.
Are passionate about scaling security through automation and best practices.

Location: India Development Center (IDC)
The Unbreakable Enterprise Kernel (UEK) team develops and maintains the Linux kernel at the heart of Oracle Linux. We build performance, reliability, and security improvements for demanding enterprise and cloud workloads. Our engineers tackle complex kernel challenges across hardware platforms, partnering with teams across software, firmware, and infrastructure. Join us to solve deep systems problems and help deliver a dependable foundation for Cloud Infrastructure at scale.
We are seeking a Linux Kernel Engineer to help develop, maintain, and secure the kernel software that supports our infrastructure. In this role, you will investigate complex systems issues, review and deliver kernel changes, and collaborate with engineers across regions to improve reliability, performance, and security.
Key responsibilities
Develop, debug, test, and maintain Linux kernel code and patches.
Review kernel changes for correctness, maintainability, performance, and regression risk.
Assess security vulnerabilities, including CVEs, and backport, validate, and deliver fixes.
Investigate kernel crashes, performance bottlenecks, and production issues using debugging and tracing tools.
Collaborate with engineering, security, and operations teams to prioritize issues and deliver timely resolutions.
Contribute to follow-the-sun operational support through clear documentation and effective handoffs across regions.
Improve testing, automation, and engineering workflows to support a growing kernel workload.
Required qualifications
Strong proficiency in C and practical experience developing or maintaining Linux kernel software.
Solid understanding of operating system fundamentals, including memory management, concurrency, synchronization, and process scheduling.
Experience diagnosing complex systems issues using crash dumps, logs, tracing, and debugging tools.
Familiarity with kernel patch review, backporting, testing, and regression analysis.
Experience using Git and collaborating on large codebases.
Ability to independently own engineering tasks, communicate technical findings clearly, and work effectively with distributed teams.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience of 6+ years.
Preferred qualifications
Contributions to the upstream Linux kernel or other systems software projects.
Experience with enterprise Linux distributions and kernel maintenance across multiple versions.
Experience assessing and remediating kernel CVEs.
Knowledge of virtualization, networking, storage, or device drivers.
Experience supporting production infrastructure and building automated kernel validation tools.
What success looks like
You deliver well-tested kernel changes, resolve complex issues, and help maintain timely security patching. Your work strengthens kernel reliability and supports effective collaboration and operational coverage across regions.
Key Responsibilities
Owns complex system modules and fleet automation workflows; defines integration contracts across software, firmware, and hardware.
Leads deep-dive investigations into incidents and hard faults; creates durable fixes and preventive controls.
Designs performance, reliability, and fault-tolerance improvements for drivers, services, and provisioning pipelines at scale.
Elevates code quality through reviews, patterns, and tooling; sets standards for observability, security, and compliance.
Guides platform bring-up and diagnostics; collaborates with silicon, board, and firmware partners to validate end-to-end behavior.

Diagnoses cross-domain issues spanning firmware, hardware, operating systems, and bootloaders using logic analyzers, JTAG, and emulators.
Participates in schematic and board reviews; leads initial board and device bring-up.
Develops and debugs advanced features—including RAS, high-speed I/O, and chipset/SoC services—across ARM, AMD, Intel, and custom ASIC/FPGA platforms.
Systems Software Development:
Design, develop, and maintain complex system software modules for managing, monitoring, and provisioning kernel and operating system software for computer servers, storage, networking, and GPU subsystems in hyperscale environment.
Utilizes advanced knowledge to design, develop, and deploy software layers and tooling to automate hardware provisioning and onboarding of servers to large-scale fleet.
Play a significant role in platform bring-up, firmware updates, platform-level diagnostics, and complex cross-layer debugging.
Diagnose and resolve complex issues across software, firmware, and hardware layers, working in DevOps and incident response paradigms to maintain reliability and availability.
Software Development and Coding:
Designs software solutions and analyzes and identifies requirements to achieve business and operational goals, sharing results with manager upon completion.
Adheres to and improves execution of all phases of the software development lifecycle; provides guidance and coaching to engineers to drive improvements.
Utilizes advanced knowledge to develop and guide new software features and enhancements leading design specifications, ensuring accessibility, and develops documents to clarify software design and code.
Leads code reviews in multiple areas to help drive improvements.
Conducts debugging and troubleshooting to identify and fix complex software issues.
Develops fixes for identified issues.
Implements comprehensive software testing (e.g., functional and non-functional testing), quality assurance processes, software error logging, monitoring, and observability for effective debugging, sharing work with manager and/or lead upon completion.
Conducts performance profiling and optimization of coding, building scalable solutions, and anticipating and resolving potential outcomes.
Troubleshoots and resolves complex issues related to application programming interface (API) functionality and integration. Implements complex API versioning, lifecycle, and interoperability strategies.
Software Architecture - Software System Structural Design:
Implements and contributes to developing software, systems, and services, ensuring review by manager and/or senior technical leaders upon completion. Recommends project or design scope.
Provides technical guidance and coaching to less experienced developers in existing software architecture.
Contributes to periodic reviews and ensures adherence to architectural standards.
Collaborates with stakeholders and networks externally to ensure work aligns with software architecture.
Implements complex performance optimization and scalability strategies in software design.
Occasionally conducts technology research and evaluation for potential architectural changes that may have an impact on results for the team.
Issue/Defect Collaboration - Software Products Support:
Collaborates with stakeholders to understand customer issues and align solutions.
May provide advanced technical guidance and support to customers regarding customer-reported issues.
Advocates for customers' interests and suggests product enhancements based on feedback.
Provides input to ensure customer satisfaction through timely resolution of issues and effective communication.
Identifies and implements customer issue and/or defect handling and training processes.
Investigates and troubleshoots complex and broad reaching/scoped maintenance issues to ensure customer agreement on short- and long-term solutions (e.g., future enhancements).
Practices and Standards Compliance - Security and Compliance:
Collaborates with the team and externally to follow development practices and coding standards, providing coaching to less experienced team members.
Participates in peer review processes, provides technical leadership, and ensures code quality and adherence to broad acceptance criteria during development, independently.
Demonstrates and shares advanced knowledge of industry best practices and applies them to software development processes.
Implements complex secure coding practices to prevent security vulnerabilities.
Development Operations - System Maintenance:
Performs periodic maintenance and testing operations for systems that require upgrading or patching (e.g., for critical vulnerabilities), sharing results with manager upon completion.
Drives improvements, ensures automation, testing, and debugging of systems to ensure service/product availability, health, support, and reliability.
Core Responsibilities
Planning & Execution:
Manages and coordinates moderately complex tasks, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure timely completion and adherence to requirements for a moderately sized project or initiative.
Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.
Collaboration & Partnership:
Collaborates across the organization to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives.
Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs.
Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.
Problem Solving:
Identifies and addresses moderately complex issues by analyzing a wide range of data and/or information to identify solutions in accordance with standard practices.
Proactively escalates unresolved or critical issues with a thorough assessment and suggests potential solutions.
Reviews, contributes to, and documents problem solving strategies.
Continuous Learning:
Pursues learning opportunities to expand knowledge and skills and/or tools in new areas and stays abreast of the latest industry trends and best practices.
Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills.
Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.
Continuous Improvement:
Develops ideas, recommends updates, and/or collaborates on the implementation of process improvements to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows across teams, and evaluates the impact on key stakeholders.
Solicits feedback from others on ideas for alternative approaches and methods for continued improvement.
Performance and Development:
Contributes to the talent development pipeline by participating in candidate interviews, assessing candidates, and providing hiring recommendations.

Memory Design Engineer

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. You have spent years in the analog and mixed-signal trenches, designing memory circuits that have to work across voltage corners, temperature extremes, and process variations without a second chance. At Synopsys, you will design embedded memories that ship in our IP portfolio and power chips across the industry.
What You'll Be Doing
Design and develop embedded CMOS memories including single-port SRAM, dual-port SRAM, register files, and ROM for Synopsys IP products
Own circuit architecture and transistor-level implementation for ultra-high-speed, ultra-low-power, or high-density memory configurations
Perform schematic entry, SPICE simulation, layout planning, and supervise physical layout execution through to final verification
Develop and verify bitcells, define layout rules, and drive layout design and parasitic extraction closure with the physical design team
Interface with CAD teams to integrate memory designs into compiler automation flows and generate EDA models for customer use

Mentor junior engineers and lead technical aspects of memory design projects from concept to delivery

The bitcells and architectures you develop will define performance, power, and area benchmarks for next-generation embedded memory IP
Your layout planning and verification rigor will reduce tapeout risk and speed time to market for memory compiler releases
The automation flows you help define will enable faster, more reliable memory generation for customers across process nodes
Your technical mentorship will build design capability within the team and raise the quality bar for future memory products

Your collaboration with CAD and frontend teams will improve tooling, models, and verification coverage across the memory IP portfolio
What You'll Need
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related technical field
Deep hands-on experience with CMOS memory circuit design including SRAM, register files, or ROM
Proficiency with circuit simulation tools such as HSPICE, Spectre, or similar SPICE-based simulators
Strong understanding of memory layout design, parasitic extraction, and layout verification tools like Calibre or Assura
Scripting capability in C-Shell, Perl, or similar languages; experience with C++ or JavaScript is a plus
Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and mentor junior engineers through complex design challenges
Experience working with memory compiler flows, EDA model generation, or design automation is a strong plus
Who You Are
You can look at a bitcell schematic and immediately spot a read stability issue or a leakage path without running a full simulation
You know how to work with layout designers, not just hand off a schematic and hope for the best, you review floorplans, flag routing issues, and iterate together

jobs.title: Staff Engineer - Subsystem Interoperability & AI-Driven Verification
jobs.description:
Job Title:
Staff Engineer - Subsystem Interoperability & AI-Driven Verification
Location- Bangalore
We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You are a verification engineer who thinks in systems, across IP blocks. You understand where interoperability problems show up: architectural boundaries, configurations, initialization sequences, protocol interactions, firmware dependencies, clock and reset domains, implementation constraints, and assumptions made between independently developed IP. Deep hands-on verification skill sits alongside the judgment to shape methodology and influence interface and testbench decisions with partner teams. You are equally comfortable building a subsystem verification environment, reviewing SystemVerilog/UVM code, analyzing coverage, debugging a difficult Controller-PHY interaction in Verdi, writing Python automation, and explaining the technical tradeoff to architects and partner teams. You turn interoperability failures into subsystem fixes that prevent the same class of issue in later configurations. The hardest cross-IP investigations are the work you want, because a clear root cause becomes a test, a check, or a design change that protects customers. At Synopsys, you will verify subsystem interoperability across high-speed interface IPs, and you will apply GenAI, LLMs, and agentic workflows so qualification is continuous and backed by evidence.
What You'll Be Doing
Drive subsystem interoperability verification across Controller, PHY, firmware, VIP, verification environments, and customer configurations for one or more high-speed interface IP families
Design and build the verification content and flows for a scalable Interop Verification Platform: continuous integration, verification, and qualification across IP releases, covering the configuration space of Controller × PHY × Firmware × VIP × Protocol Mode × Customer Configuration, and using risk and coverage to decide what must be qualified
Develop reusable verification architectures, methodologies, and reference environments for functional verification, protocol compliance, error and stress scenarios, coverage, assertions, CDC/RDC, and system initialization
Own the hardest cross-IP investigations and drive fixes across RTL, PHY, firmware, VIP, testbench, and implementation boundaries when interoperability issues appear
Work with Controller and PHY architects and R&D teams early in the lifecycle on interfaces, observability, design-for-verification, and subsystem behavior
Apply GenAI, LLMs, RAG, and agentic workflows to the verification work this team owns, from specification and verification intent through environment, tests, regression, debug, qualification, and what the team learns from each failure
Build AI-assisted flows for environment and test generation, regression selection, log and failure clustering, coverage-gap analysis, protocol and waveform debug, root-cause recommendations, engineering knowledge retrieval, and qualification evidence
The Impact You Will Have
Make interoperability a continuous part of development for the subsystems you own, so bring-up and qualification start earlier and finish with evidence
Verify a growing set of IP configurations so Controller-PHY combinations are exercised before they reach a customer environment
Turn field and integration issues into permanent tests and shared debug knowledge, so the same failure does not return and the team keeps the lesson
Contribute reusable interoperability methods across the protocols you work on, including UCIe, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet, DDR/HBM, USB, and AMBA/CHI
Apply an AI-assisted verification flow so debug skill and methodology extend across more products and configurations
Produce compatibility matrices and qualification evidence that show when a specific Controller-PHY combination is ready for customers, and shorten integration time
Mentor other engineers and raise the quality of environments, reviews, and debug on the team
What You'll Need
5+ years of ASIC, IP, or SoC verification experience, with ownership of complex verification work and a record of influencing design and verification decisions with partner teams. Senior Staff candidates also show broader scope: reusable architectures or methodologies adopted beyond a single project, and technical leadership of interoperability work across configurations or teams
Deep expertise in SystemVerilog, UVM, assertions, functional and code coverage, verification closure, and complex debug, including building and reviewing sophisticated verification environments
Experience creating reusable verification environments for IP, subsystem, or SoC designs that other engineers could pick up and extend
Strong expertise in one or more high-speed protocols such as UCIe, PCIe/CXL, Ethernet, DDR/HBM, USB, or AMBA/CHI, including protocol interactions, initialization sequences, and interoperability issues
Hands-on use of industry simulation and debug tools, VIP, and coverage infrastructure, specifically VCS and Verdi or an equivalent toolchain
Automation skill in Python, Tcl, or a similar language, with examples of scripts or tools that made verification faster or more reliable
Experience with CDC/RDC, formal verification, emulation or prototyping, CI/CD, or distributed regression infrastructure is an advantage, as is experience or a demonstrated interest in GenAI, LLMs, RAG, agentic workflows, and AI-assisted verification
Who You Are
You can join a Controller-PHY integration that is failing in a customer configuration, debug the waveforms in Verdi, find the root cause across firmware, RTL, and protocol assumptions, and define the fix that prevents the same issue in later configurations
You align partner teams through technical credibility, clear communication, and a record of closing hard problems
You mentor other engineers by teaching them how to structure a verification environment and how to reason about a subsystem failure
You move between hands-on work and technical planning: reviewing a UVM testbench, proposing the verification approach for the next release, and walking architects through a risk in the interface or the initialization sequence
You treat AI and LLMs as practical tools for scaling verification, and you are ready to apply GenAI from specification through qualification on the work this team owns
You raise concerns when an interface creates interoperability risk or a qualification plan has no evidence behind it, because the subsystem has to work in the customer's configuration
The Team You'll Be Part Of
You will work in the IP R&D organization at Synopsys with Controller and PHY architects, verification engineers, firmware engineers, and VIP developers across high-speed interface IP families. Your work sits where these teams meet: you own interoperability verification and help define the checks, environments, and evidence that show a subsystem works as a subsystem. You will collaborate with engineers in Bangalore and at other R&D sites. The role is hands-on and technical. Customer-ready Controller-PHY combinations depend on the quality of this work.
Rewards and Benefits
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.
At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.
